prompt: Current state of CRISPR gene therapy approvals and ongoing clinical trials
report:
# CRISPR Gene Therapy: Approvals and Trials

## Approved therapies
The first CRISPR-Cas9 therapy, Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel), was approved by the FDA and MHRA in late 2023 for sickle-cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia [S1][S2]. It edits the BCL11A enhancer to reactivate fetal hemoglobin [S3].

## Ongoing clinical trials
Multiple clinical trial programs are advancing in-vivo editing: Intellia's NTLA-2001 targets transthyretin amyloidosis with a single infusion [S4][S5], and trials for hereditary angioedema report durable knockdown [S6]. Base- and prime-editing candidates are entering first-in-human clinical trial phases [S7].

## Safety and off-target effects
The central safety concern remains off-target edits and large deletions at the Cas9 cut site [S8][S9]. Newer high-fidelity Cas9 variants and off-target screening assays (GUIDE-seq) reduce but do not eliminate the risk [S9][S10].

## Outlook
Approvals validate ex-vivo CRISPR-Cas9; the frontier is safe in-vivo delivery with minimal off-target activity [S5][S8].
